input_domain.value: Accept valid caller inputs with a nonempty sessionID, at least one available option, unique ASCII option IDs matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]+, nonempty copy, and caller-preserved option order; the component owns no audio engine or network operation.

identifiers.value: Expose stable identifiers listening.canvas, listening.title, listening.introduction, listening.note, listening.acknowledge, listening.status, listening.primary, listening.cancel, listening.footer, listening.error and listening.summary; each option control uses listening.option.<id>.

semantics.value: Give each option one native button with accessible label title + " — " + detail and a selected trait that matches its local selection; the acknowledgement is one labeled native switch with its real Boolean value.

selection.value: Selecting an available option exclusively selects its ID; selecting it again preserves that selection, changing to another available option replaces it, and unavailable options remain disabled and never selectable.

validation.value: While editing, a successful Start listening activation validates both an available selected option and acknowledgement on; unmet conditions leave editing active and show the applicable exact error text defined in api-contract.json without emitting onStart or onCancel. Exact error copy: {"acknowledgement": "Confirm the quiet-space note before starting.", "both": "Choose a soundscape and confirm the quiet-space note.", "selection": "Choose an available soundscape."}

cancel.value: Cancel remains enabled in every state; each activation invokes onCancel(current sessionID) once and returns to initial editing for that same input, including repeated Cancel activations with no choices.

edit_error.value: Changing either editing choice clears the visible validation error; turning acknowledgement off is allowed while editing and does not clear the selected option.

replacement.value: Any unequal full input replacement resets selection, acknowledgement, validation and started state before the replacement is rendered, even when sessionID and option IDs are unchanged; rendering an equal input preserves local state and neither case emits callbacks.

bridge_boundary.value: Keep the component identity and business logic in production: the supplied bridges adapt fixture values and real callback arguments only, and neither bridge may force identity changes, supply local product state, or synthesize callback outcomes.

colors.value: Use exact opaque sRGB colors from reference.json: canvas behind the column and Cancel; option/selectedOption/unavailableOption on option surfaces; primary and primaryInk on the primary button; title on the heading; body on introduction, note, available option titles, acknowledgement, status, summary and Cancel text; muted on option details, unavailable option titles and footer; error on error text; border on every option outline; use no shadows, gradients or translucency.

spacing.value: Use a single column filling its parent content width (the observer offers total width minus its own 32-unit horizontal inset), with 20 native units of internal canvas padding, 12 units between major blocks and options, 12-unit option and action corner radii, 16-unit option/action horizontal padding and 12-unit vertical padding, and a 1-unit option border; each title/detail option pair has a 4-unit internal gap and actions fill the available column width.

typography.value: Use platform-scaled system text at the base sizes and weights in reference.json: title 24 semibold, introduction/note/option title 16 regular except option title semibold, option detail/footer 14 regular, status/error/summary 16 regular, and action text 16 semibold.

evidence.value: Keep source font and padding review separate from native rectangle and text facts: AX bounds do not establish computed font, padding, color or physical hit regions.

callback_evidence.value: The six route checkpoints and all assertions are fixed before implementation; callback verdicts require demonstrated successful dispatch to exactly one enabled native control in one input epoch, or demonstrated same-process caller replacement for caller_update, before comparing the exact callback interval.

callback_boundaries.value: Only valid Start listening and Cancel activations invoke the supplied callbacks; selection changes, acknowledgement changes, validation failures, Choose again, recomposition and caller replacements invoke neither callback, and each actual action uses the callbacks supplied by the current caller.

native_matrix.value: The complete native rule/state matrix is owned by R04, R06, R07, R10, R11, R12, R21 and R26. Every applicable cell is independently specified by typed source pointers; conditional text absent in a state has an explicit N/A label cell and an assessed presence rule.

checkpoint_validation.value: Activate Start listening with neither requirement satisfied; show both-condition error.

checkpoint_started.value: Choose the first available option, turn acknowledgement on, then Start listening; one start callback.

checkpoint_renewed.value: Activate Choose again; empty editing state and no callback.

checkpoint_canceled.value: Choose the second available option, acknowledge, then Cancel; one cancel callback and empty editing state.

checkpoint_replaced.value: Make editing dirty with the first option and acknowledgement, then replace the entire input without remounting; new copy, empty local state, no callback.

acknowledgement.value: I have read the quiet-space note

ready.value: Choose a soundscape for your break.

title.value: A small pocket of quiet between the busy parts of your day

introduction.value: Settle in at your own pace and choose a recording that feels comfortable today. Every soundscape has its own rhythm, and you are welcome to change your mind before beginning this listening break.

quietNote.value: Before starting, make sure you are somewhere you can rest without needing to watch for moving traffic, equipment, or other demands on your attention. Keep the volume comfortable enough to notice your surroundings, and stop the break whenever you need to.

footer.value: A listening break is simply an invitation to pause. There is no score to achieve, no timer you must complete, and no need to keep a particular pace. Your choice belongs to this local session, and this panel does not begin audio playback.

status.value: Choose a soundscape for your break.

error.value: Choose a soundscape and confirm the quiet-space note.

summary.value: Ready to begin: A winding woodland brook after the overnight rain

option_a.value: A winding woodland brook after the overnight rain — Water moves over shallow stones while occasional birds call from deeper in the trees. There is no narration and no music, so the sound can leave plenty of space for your own thoughts.

option_b.value: A warm room beside the old library fireplace — Low crackles, a little movement in the room, and quiet intervals between them. The recording was made from an armchair a comfortable distance from the fire.

unavailable.value: The far meadow beyond the orchard wall — This longer field recording is being prepared for the collection and cannot be selected yet. Another available soundscape can be chosen now.

obligations.clause: Display this exact vertical order: input title, introduction, all option title/detail pairs in caller order, quietNote, fixed acknowledgement switch, status, conditional error, conditional success summary, primary action, Cancel action, and footer; display all caller copy verbatim.

Give each option one native button with accessible label title + " — " + detail and a selected trait that matches its local selection; the acknowledgement is one labeled native switch with its real Boolean value.
Begin editing with no selection, acknowledgement off, no error or success summary, status "Choose a soundscape for your break.", and enabled Start listening and Cancel controls.

On valid Start listening activation, enter the started state synchronously, show status "Your listening break is ready.", show summary "Ready to begin: " + selected option title, and invoke onStart(sessionID, optionID) exactly once for that activation.

In the started state, retain all caller content, preserve the selected option and on acknowledgement, disable every option and the acknowledgement, and change the enabled primary label to "Choose again".
A Choose again activation returns to the initial editing state for the current input, clears selection, acknowledgement, errors and summary, and emits no callbacks.
Render the component canvas in its canvas role color throughout all states and the primary button in its primary role color in both Start listening and Choose again states.

Give the primary and Cancel native accessible/control rectangles minimum height 48 native units and minimum width 120 native units; option rectangles have minimum height 64 native units and may grow for content or text size.

Allow all supplied copy and action labels to wrap without truncation, ellipsis, text scaling down, horizontal scrolling, clipping, or overlap; use leading alignment and let the parent vertical scroller reach every item at offered widths 320 through 430 and system text sizes through iOS accessibility2 / Android fontScale 1.6.

At every route checkpoint the visible content must be complete and mutually non-overlapping, including validation and success text when present; the canvas and primary color, content presence, wrapping and overlap are independent review atoms.

For the route, an invalid Start emits no events, a valid Start emits only the selected start event, Choose again emits no events, Cancel emits only its cancel event, and dirty-state caller replacement emits no events and displays only the new copy with reset local choices.
Native labels, enabled state, selection, toggle value, conditional presence and geometry match the fixed complete per-state matrix.

trust_limit: Identity and exact typed derivation only. Authorship, design correctness and approval require a separate preimplementation review record.
